text:
alex: Heads-up question for routing + docs: were finalizing the /v1/generate contract and need to be explicit about how model selection params interplay (model_id, model_hint, region_hint, tier_hint). Can we confirm exact precedence and what clients should expect in responses?

sara: Precedence today (short): model_id > pinned_version > model_hint > route_catalog_default. model_hint is advisory unless tenant opts into strict matching.

mike: Routing rules from infra perspective: if model_id present -> try exact variant in requested region/tier. If unavailable: behavior depends on tenant flag `strict_model_matching`.

mike: - strict_model_matching=true -> return 400 {"error":"model_not_available","suggestions":[...]}
mike: - strict_model_matching=false -> perform compatibility fallback (see matrix). We try minimal-latency compatible substitutes first.

nina: Compatibility fallback (ordered):
```
1) exact ID in same region/tier
2) same family & compatible arch, same region/tier
3) same family & compatible arch, different tier in same region
4) cross-region compatible variant (only if region_fallback=true)
5) route default model (catalog default)
```

alex: Good. semantics for region_hint/tier_hint? Are they enforced or just preferences?

sara: By default they are preferences. Add `must_match_region=true` or `must_match_tier=true` to enforce (will 400 if no match). Note: private deployments default `region_fallback=false` and stricter policies.

alex: Need a canonical example for docs and SDKs. Draft payload?

mike: Example request we should include in docs:
```
POST /v1/generate
{
  "model_id": "redwood-llama-7b-q4",
  "model_hint": "llama-2-70b",
  "region_hint": "eu-west-1",
  "tier_hint": "standard",
  "region_fallback": true
}
```

mike: And example response when we routed to a substitute (important: clients must log this if they care about exact model economics):
```
{
  "id": "gen_xxx",
  "model": "redwood-llama-7b-q4",
  "routed_model_id": "llama-2-70b-q4o",
  "meta": {"compat_path": ["requested:redwood-llama-7b-q4","routed:llama-2-70b-q4o"]}
}
```

sara: Docs note: `routed_model_id` is informational unless strict_model_matching is enabled. Also add that we surface `compat_path` and a `routed_reason` code for telemetry.

alex: Backwards compatibility: older clients send `model` instead of `model_id`. Do we still accept that?

mike: Yes, `model` is aliased to `model_id` for now. We'll add an `X-Deprecation-Notice: model -> model_id` header starting 3 months from canary. We'll announce migration plan.

nina: I'll make sure evals + cost telemetry ingest `routed_model_id` and tag traces so we can detect quality regressions after fallbacks.

deploy-bot: Deploy scheduled: routing-service v2.14 -> canary 2026-03-18T02:00Z, full rollout 2026-03-19 (monitoring window 24h).

alex: OK. Action items: sara adds the example request/response to eng-platform docs and tags me; mike updates tenant feature flags docs and coordinates account team; nina hooks routed_model_id into telemetry; I'll update SDK PRs to surface routed_model_id in debug logs. Ping here if anything changes during canary.

sara: On it, opening docs PR now :thumbsup:

mike: Will add strict_model_matching flag note and deprecation header to changelog.

nina: Copy, I'll run a quick eval sweep against canary to validate output quality for the fallback path.

alex: Thanks everyone.
